summary: Researched the evening before (Mon 16 Nov) under the stricter rules; lineups are not out, so this is a draft until the morning check and the final check. Tuesday has the last Nations League matchday for the other groups and a EuroLeague round. Ten games were researched: four are kept at medium, four at low, and two are excluded; the rest were not reached. Medium: BC Dubai v Anadolu Efes (p 0.74; Dubai at their regular home arena, Efes without Mike James, Cordinier and Bruno Fernando; Dubai miss three forwards and just lost by 29), Hapoel Tel Aviv at Baskonia (p 0.60; Baskonia are 1-11 with three injured and two new signings; Hapoel have lost three straight; the Polymarket market is thin, and bookmakers rate Hapoel higher at 71-74%), Zalgiris v Bayern (p 0.79; Zalgiris on a five-game winning streak against the league's worst defence; point guard Williams-Goss out), Hungary v Northern Ireland (p 0.46, draw 0.31, so only double chance or goals legs; Northern Ireland need just a draw to win the group and have not conceded in five games). Low, so not bet: Virtus v Panathinaikos (Panathinaikos's price fell 6.5% with no news), Barcelona v Paris (Barcelona's price fell 12% with no news, four players out), Wales v Portugal (Portugal miss Dias, Mendes, Bernardo Silva and possibly Palhinha; sources conflict), Ireland v Kosovo (no team news or lineups found). Excluded: Maccabi Tel Aviv v Olympiacos (Maccabi's home games are played in Limassol, Cyprus: neutral venue), Bosnia v Romania (Bosnia's second place is already fixed while Romania need a win to avoid the relegation play-off). Morning check (Tue): no new team news overnight. Hapoel's price rose from 62% to 77% with no news, the thin Polymarket market catching up with the bookmakers (71-74%); kept at medium. Zalgiris's price fell 3.7% since first listing with no news to explain it, so it is now low. Dubai (-2.6%, injury lists unchanged) and Hungary (price stable, same suspensions) stay medium. Four more games checked in the morning: Panathinaikos stays low (its price fell 6.5% on Monday and rose 11% overnight, with no news for either move); Bnei Herzliya v Bonn is excluded (Herzliya's home game is played in Samokov, Bulgaria: neutral venue); Roma v Bahcesehir and Balkan v Ulm are low (no injury news, no second bookmaker price, thin markets). Afternoon check (Tue 14:25 UTC): no new injuries. Dubai stay medium (price back to 76.5%, returners unconfirmed); Hapoel stay medium (Satoransky back, Caboclo probably out, the price fell from 76.5% to 70.5% this afternoon with no news but is still above its first listing and inside the bookmakers' 71-74.5%); Hungary stay medium (price stable, DraftKings and bet365 agree, official XI not out before the first leg starts); Zalgiris stay low (no fresh bookmaker price to confirm the recovery). The slip now starts at 19:30 UTC (Hapoel), so the final check moves to about 18:00 UTC; bet only after it.

checks.team_news: Afternoon re-check (about 14:30 UTC) found nothing new. Zalgiris: Nigel Williams-Goss (thigh) out for both games this week per coach Masiulis (BasketNews.lt, morning finding still holds); Keenan Evans is cover; no other Zalgiris absence found. Bayern: Austin Wiley (hip) uncertain per German press, travelled to Kaunas; no confirmation either way. English and Lithuanian searches this afternoon returned only older-season items. Today's EuroLeague injury report was not readable (euroleaguebasketball.net returned 429 earlier, not used), and fcbayern.com returned 403.
checks.lineups: Still no official or predicted starting fives found. Expected from previews (unconfirmed): Zalgiris with Evans or Jokubaitis at guard, Grigonis, Valanciunas at center; Bayern with Obst and Wiley if fit.
checks.rotation: Unchanged: Zalgiris beat Armani Milan 86-83 away (five-game winning streak) and had rest. Bayern lost 102-87 at Valencia, travelled Monday, and has a Thursday home game vs Baskonia (double week); partial rotation possible but not confirmed.
checks.motivation: Zalgiris 8th at 7-4, Bayern 18th at 3-8; both need wins.
checks.form: Zalgiris 5 straight EuroLeague wins, net rating -5.1 (3StepsBasket). Bayern 3-8, three wins all away, net rating -9.9, worst defense in the league.
checks.h2h: Zalgiris won both 2025-26 meetings (98-70 in Munich, 78-71 in Kaunas on 24 Mar 2026 per a results page); thetopbookies claims a different 3-2 Bayern record over five meetings, so h2h is a weak signal.
checks.odds: Polymarket home live 0.795 at 14:22 UTC vs 0.785 this morning (partial recovery) vs 0.815 at first listing (-2.5%, inside the 3% line) and 0.81 24h ago (-1.9%). Away 0.205. The recovery is unexplained and no news found accounts for the earlier dip either. Second source did not confirm: thetopbookies returned 429 again, so no fresh bookmaker price was seen. The only bookmaker figures are older: bet-experts (checked 15 Nov) about 1.21 / 5.75 (81% / 19%), spread -9.5, total 171.5; 1xBet via thetopbookies about 1.19 / 4.60 (79% / 21%). They predate the Polymarket move, so they cannot confirm today's price. The medium conditions (price within 3%, nothing new hurts, second price source agrees) are not all met because the second source is missing.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free model found. 3StepsBasket net-rating gap of about 4.8 plus about 3 points home court implies roughly an 8 point margin, a little under the -9.5 market line; this supports shading below the market, hence p home 0.77.
checks.venue_weather: Zalgirio Arena, Kaunas, genuine home game, Tue 17 Nov 18:00 UTC (20:00 local). Indoor, no weather issue.

games.reason: Zalgiris is at home on a five-game winning streak against the league's worst-defending side (3-8), and weekend bookmaker prices were around 79-81%. No hard exclusion applies. The live price (0.795) is within 3% of first listing (0.815) and no new bad news was found, but no fresh bookmaker price could be obtained (429 / 403 blocks) and the lineups and Wiley's status stay unconfirmed, so the check for a second agreeing price source fails and confidence stays low.
games.main_risk: The price fell about 3.7% this morning for no reason I could find and only partly recovered; no fresh bookmaker price confirms the current level; Williams-Goss is out; both teams have weak net ratings (gap about 4.8), so a close loss is plausible; Bayern's Wiley and Obst may play; lineups and the official injury report remain unseen.

checks.team_news: Afternoon re-check (BasketNews injury report stamped 17 Nov 14:10; Eurohoops R12 report 17 Nov 08:35 UTC). Dubai OUT: Bertans (hamstring), Jaiteh (Achilles rehab), Kondic (hip/psoas), Abass (not on the EuroLeague roster). BasketNews still lists Walkup EXPECTED (back in ABA League 15 Nov after missing R7-11), Anderson EXPECTED (hamstring; Eurohoops notes he debuted in the ABA League last week but did not play R11 or the domestic game at the weekend), Huertas GAME-TIME (new signing), Prepelic UNCERTAIN (coach's decision). Eurohoops says Dubai had not yet sent an injury report for this game and names nobody as out or returning, so Walkup, Anderson, Huertas and Prepelic are all still unconfirmed at 14:25 UTC. Efes: Mike James out for the season, Cordinier out indefinitely, Fernando out 3-4 weeks (calf), all club-confirmed. New: Eurohoops says P.J. Dozier returned to action in R11, so he looks available, though the EuroLeague game page snippet says he is out 2-3 weeks with a back injury. I could not resolve the conflict, and BasketNews lists no Efes player as expected back. Dozier playing would be a small plus for Efes. No late illness or coach comments found. euroleaguebasketball.net game notes returned 429 and were not used.
checks.lineups: No official or predicted starting fives yet; official XIs come after this check. Dubai's availability list is not confirmed by the club.
checks.rotation: Unchanged: Dubai at home with 4-5 days rest after the 101-72 loss at Olympiacos; Efes played a domestic game on 15 Nov and travelled. No rotation news.
checks.motivation: Unchanged: Dubai 7-4 wanting to avoid a third home loss; Efes 5-6 needing wins.
checks.form: Unchanged: Dubai last 5 LWWLW (86.5 scored / 85.6 allowed); Efes WLWLW (85.9 / 87.5).
checks.h2h: Unchanged: split 1-1 (Dubai 80-76 at Efes Dec 2025; Efes 85-69 in Sarajevo Apr 2026).
checks.odds: Polymarket live 0.765 Dubai at 14:22 UTC. First listed 0.76, this morning 0.74, so the price has recovered 2.5 points since the morning and is +0.5 points (+0.7% relative) vs p_first. The favourite's price has not moved against it, so the low-confidence trigger is not met. The 24h move in the file is 0.76 to 0.765. No fresh bookmaker price found this afternoon (a search only surfaced basketballsphere's preview page, no numbers I could verify). The last second-source prices I have are Monday's (1xBet 1.28/3.60, de-vigged about 0.74; BetMGM 7/20), which are slightly shorter for Efes than the live Polymarket price. No Stake/Rainbet price seen.
checks.models: Unchanged: season net ratings favour Dubai by roughly 6-7 points before home court, about 73-75%, small samples.
checks.venue_weather: Unchanged: Coca-Cola Arena, Dubai, 20:00 local (16:00 UTC), indoor.

games.reason: Fixture and venue verified; no hard exclusion. Dubai remain favourites at home against an Efes side missing Mike James (season), Cordinier and Fernando, while Dubai lack Bertans, Jaiteh and Kondic. The live price (0.765) is back above the first listing, so no adverse move. Dubai's returners (Walkup, Anderson, Huertas, Prepelic) are unconfirmed and P.J. Dozier may be available for Efes, so p is held at 0.74, below the market, and confidence stays medium.
games.main_risk: Dubai have not confirmed who is available (Walkup, Anderson and Prepelic are still unconfirmed; Huertas is game-time), they are thin up front (Bertans, Jaiteh, Kondic out) and inconsistent (lost 101-72 at Olympiacos, two home losses already). P.J. Dozier may have returned for Efes. The bookmaker price could not be refreshed, only Monday's. If Walkup and Anderson are ruled out, or the price slides before tip-off, the leg is weaker.

checks.team_news: Re-checked this morning (Tue 17 Nov) in English, Italian and Greek. No current injury, illness, return or suspension report found for either side, and no Monday press-conference or media-day comments for Round 12. Results were only older seasons: Nunn/Holmes/Lessort items from Oct 2025 and Jan 2026, Edwards ankle (late 2025), and Brown flu in Nov 2024. Status of Nunn, Holmes and Virtus's roster for tonight is still unverified. Nothing new this morning explains the price move.
checks.lineups: Not available. No expected starting fives found for either side this morning; official lineups are for the final check.
checks.rotation: Unchanged from last night. Panathinaikos beat Real Madrid 115-112 in OT on 4 Nov (Eurohoops). Schedule since, and Virtus's recent schedule, not verified.
checks.motivation: Early-season regular-season game (Round 12). Panathinaikos were 8-2 after round 10 per a sportschau snapshot; Virtus's record not confirmed. No hard-exclusion situation applies.
checks.form: Panathinaikos 8-2 after round 10 and won 115-112 in OT at Real Madrid (4 Nov). Full last 6-10 results and home/away splits not found.
checks.h2h: Last season: Virtus won 92-75 at home on 24 Oct 2025 (Sky Sport); Panathinaikos won 84-71 in Athens on 8 Jan 2026 (Sky Sport). Virtus has beaten Panathinaikos at home before, so an upset is not remote.
checks.odds: Polymarket Panathinaikos: first listed 0.71, last night 0.71 (0.715), live now 0.79 (24h move 0.725 to 0.795, +9.7% relative; +11% vs last night). It fell about 6.5% on Monday and rose about 10-11% overnight with no news found for either swing, so the swings are unexplained both ways. Only bookmaker data found: a BasketballSphere preview dated 15 Nov listing Panathinaikos -8.5 at 1.72 and Virtus +9.5 at 1.78 (22bet). That is a handicap line, not a moneyline price. It shows a clear Panathinaikos favourite but cannot be de-vigged or compared with 0.79, and I did not open the full article. No Stake or Rainbet price seen.
checks.models: No net rating, power ranking or model prediction found for this game; data.rating is absent.
checks.venue_weather: Virtus Segafredo Arena, Bologna (home venue). Tip 20:00 UTC (21:00 local) on Tue 17 Nov 2026; teams, date and competition confirmed (ticket-compare, BasketballSphere preview). Indoor, weather irrelevant.

games.reason: Fixture verified and no hard exclusion, but the price swung down 6.5% on Monday and up about 10-11% overnight with no team news found for either move. No injury, lineup or press-conference information and no moneyline from a second bookmaker (only a -8.5 handicap that points the same way). Per the brief, medium needs clear team news and bookmakers agreeing with the live price, so it stays low. p is shaded about 3 points below the live 0.79.
games.main_risk: Unexplained two-way price volatility on Panathinaikos (0.765 to 0.715 to 0.79) with team news unknown. A late absence such as Nunn or Holmes could be behind it. Virtus at home beat Panathinaikos 92-75 in Oct 2025.

games.reason: HARD rule: neutral/unusual venue. Maccabi's EuroLeague home games are not played in Tel Aviv. EuroLeague approved the Spyros Kyprianou Arena in Limassol, Cyprus as Maccabi's home venue until further notice, starting with Round 11 (Hapoel game on 12 Nov 2026), per Eurohoops and Cyprus Mail on 4 Nov 2026. The 17 Nov game is Round 12, so it falls under this arrangement and is a home game played abroad. The Polymarket favourite price also jumped from 0.43 to 0.695 in 24h (+61.6% relative), which I could not explain from the venue news alone.
games.main_risk: Home game played abroad in Limassol (neutral venue, no real home advantage); also an unexplained 24h price jump on Olympiacos (0.43 to 0.695).

checks.team_news: Portugal: Ruben Dias suspended (yellow vs Denmark), Joao Palhinha also reported suspended (Goal), Nuno Mendes injured, Bernardo Silva sent home as physically unfit (Goal) / a knock (Portugoal), Cancelo back from suspension. Portugal's first match since Cristiano Ronaldo's official farewell. Wales (Sports Mole, 16 Nov): Ethan Ampadu suspended, Neco Williams injured, Connor Roberts expected to replace him, David Brooks scored in Norway. Sources conflict on some Portugal absences (Palhinha is in the Portugoal predicted XI but Goal says suspended); no press conference found.
checks.lineups: Not out. Sports Mole predicted Portugal: D Costa; A Costa, A Silva, Veiga, Dalot; J Neves, Vitinha; B Silva, Felix, Fernandes; Ramos (lists B Silva although Goal says he left the camp). Portugoal predicted: D Costa, A Costa, Veiga, A Silva, Cancelo, Palhinha, B Fernandes, Vitinha, Forbs, Felix, Ramos. Sports Mole predicted Wales: Darlow; Roberts, Rodon, Davies, Dasilva; Cullen, Sheehan; Johnson, Brooks, Wilson; Koumas. Two sources disagree, so the Portugal XI is unverified.
checks.rotation: Portugal played Denmark on Sat 14 Nov (lost 1-4 at home), Wales played in Norway the same day (lost 1-3); both have 3 days' rest. Portugal travel to Cardiff. No further games before the tie-up of the group. Three or four Portugal regulars are out for reasons other than rotation (suspension, injury, fitness).
checks.motivation: Sky Sports table (updated 16 Nov 18:55), 5 played each: Portugal 12 pts (W4 L1, GF10 GA8, GD+2), Denmark 9 (GD+3), Norway 6 (GD 0), Wales 3 (GD-5). Last matchday: Wales v Portugal and Denmark v Norway on 17 Nov. Portugal cannot finish below 2nd (Denmark max 12 and Portugal already 12), but first place is NOT secured: a Portugal defeat plus a Denmark win leaves them level on 12 and Denmark won the head-to-head on aggregate (Portugal 4-2 Denmark earlier, Denmark 4-1 Portugal on 14 Nov), so Portugal need at least a draw for sure first place. Sports Mole says Portugal must avoid defeat to keep top spot. Wales are bottom with 3 pts; a win would lift them level with Norway on 6, so they still play for 3rd (relegation play-off) versus 4th (relegation); sources differ (Sports Mole: Wales need a point to secure the play-off; Portugoal: already relegated). Denmark v Norway matters: Denmark need a win and a Portugal slip for first place. Verdict: not a hard exclusion, since the favourite still needs a point; soft risk because Portugal's aim is partly secured (quarter-final place) and Wales and Denmark have more to gain.
checks.form: Portugal: five straight wins ended with the 1-4 home loss to Denmark (worst home competitive defeat per press); earlier 1-0 home win over Wales (24 Sep, Felix) and 4-2 win at Denmark. Wales: 1 win in the last 9 matches, 3-1 loss in Norway on 14 Nov (Brooks goal); Wales GF3 GA8 over 5 group games. No xG found.
checks.h2h: 24 Sep 2026 Portugal 1-0 Wales in Lisbon (Wales faced 23 shots, only a deflected Felix goal separated them). Wales are a low-scoring side so a narrow Portugal win or a draw is the main alternative path.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (data.odds): Wales 6.00, Draw 4.70, Portugal 1.42 (opening 1.40), de-vigged Wales 15.4%, draw 19.6%, Portugal 65.0%, total 3.5. Polymarket Portugal 66.5% -> 68.5% over 24h (+3% relative, a rise, so not a fall). A Wincomparator model page quotes Portugal 52.75% (commercial, unreliable). Market price of 68% is above the de-vigged 65% and above Elo (below), so p is trimmed to 65%.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net): Portugal 1996, Wales 1673, expected score for Wales 0.217 (draw counts half), which implies roughly Portugal 66-70% before depleted-squad adjustment.
checks.venue_weather: Cardiff City Stadium, Tue 17 Nov 2026, 19:45 (Sports Mole, Kickoff.co.uk); ordinary home venue. Cardiff forecast for that evening not found (searches returned undated results), so weather is unverified; no pitch problem reported. Goal's listing shows 13:45 for the time, probably in another time zone.

games.reason: Not a hard exclusion: table checked first, Portugal (12 pts) are through to the quarter-finals but still need a point to guarantee first place over Denmark (9 pts, with the head-to-head advantage), and Wales (3 pts, bottom) still have the 3rd-versus-4th relegation stakes. Portugal also lose Dias, Mendes, Bernardo Silva and possibly Palhinha, and just conceded four at home. Confidence is low because squad and lineup facts conflict across sources and are unconfirmed, the weather is unverified and Portugal's own defeat would not cost them a quarter-final place.
games.main_risk: A draw or upset: depleted Portugal (Dias suspended, Mendes injured, Bernardo Silva out, Palhinha reported suspended) after a 1-4 home loss, against a Wales side that still plays for relegation play-off survival and held Portugal to 1-0 in September; Wales have scored 3 goals in 5 group games, so a narrow 1-0 or a 0-0/1-1 draw is the likely failure for any handicap or goals leg.

checks.team_news: Barcelona: Kevin Punter (top scorer, 15.9 ppg, ankle sprain, about 6 weeks), Tosan Evbuomwan (oblique tear, about 3 weeks), Umoja Gibson (muscle strain, about 3 weeks) and Yoan Makoundou (knee) are out; Juan Nunez (right ankle sprain) is day-to-day (basketballsphere.com EuroLeague injury page updated 16 Nov; Infobae preview 16 Nov). Paris: no injured players listed; Daulton Hommes missed rounds 9-10 and returned in the French league at the weekend. No Barcelona press-conference quote found, so Nunez's status is unconfirmed.
checks.lineups: Not out yet. Infobae (16 Nov) probable fives: Barcelona Robinson, Brizuela, Parra, Martin, Nebo (Nunez on the bench list, not a starter); Paris Hifi, Herrera, Warren, Dokossi, Faye. Only one source found for the XIs, so they are unconfirmed.
checks.rotation: Barcelona won 76-74 at Panathinaikos in round 11 (Thursday, about 4 days' rest, a Barcelona win after a 3-day trip to Athens), then host Paris on Tue 17 Nov (round 12). Paris beat Fenerbahce 111-109 in overtime on Wed 11 Nov at home and played the French league at the weekend, so they have a similar rest. The kickoff is listed as 20:30 Spanish time (19:30 UTC). I did not find either side's next fixture.
checks.motivation: EuroLeague standings after round 11 (Wikipedia, through 13 Nov): 1 Valencia 8-3, 2 Panathinaikos 8-3, 3 Olympiacos 8-3, 4 Barcelona 8-3 (+30), 5 Real Madrid 7-4 ... 12 Anadolu 5-6, 13 Besiktas 5-6, 14 Paris 5-6 (-36). Both want wins; Barcelona are in the top-4 race, Paris are chasing the play-in places. Nothing is secured, so no hard exclusion.
checks.form: Barcelona: 8-3, 978 points for, 948 against (+30); 3-2 at home; won 93-90 at Hapoel on 5 Nov and 76-74 at Panathinaikos in round 11, both close. Justin Robinson has scored 10 or more in 8 straight games. Paris: 5-6, 982 for, 1018 against (-36); four straight wins, including 95-90 at Efes and the 111-109 overtime win over Fenerbahce; Hifi leads the league in scoring (20.8 ppg) and Paris have the third-best offence (about 91 ppg).
checks.h2h: The road team won all of the last four Barcelona-Paris meetings by double digits, including Paris 85-74 at the Palau in Feb 2026 and 103-87 in Nov 2024 (Infobae preview; EuroLeague game notes). That is a poor sign for a home favourite, though the squads have changed.
checks.odds: Polymarket moneyline for Barcelona: 0.73 at 20:00 UTC on 15 Nov, 0.72 at 11:00 UTC on 16 Nov, then a drop to 0.65 at 12:00 UTC and 0.64 now (move_24h 0.73 to 0.64, -12.3% relative). I found no news that explains it: the Punter, Evbuomwan and Gibson absences were already known, so the confidence is low under the price-move rule. Other books: FanDuel (search snippet) Barcelona -380 / Paris +280, spread Barcelona -8.5, which de-vigs to about 75% / 25% for Barcelona; bet-experts quotes Barcelona about 1.34-1.37 and Paris +7.5 at 1.93. The books are well above Polymarket's 64%, and I could not tell how current the snippets are. Polymarket spread Barcelona -8.5 is priced at 0.23 and the total at 185.5 is 50/50. I did not find a Stake or Rainbet price.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating, such as net rating or a power ranking, was found for this season. Point difference per game from the Wikipedia table: Barcelona +2.7 (+30 over 11), Paris -3.3 (-36 over 11), a gap of about 6 points per game, plus home court for Barcelona. This points to a Barcelona edge of roughly 6-8 points, and Paris's offence is strong, so the gap is not safe.
checks.venue_weather: Palau Blaugrana, Barcelona, is Barcelona's normal home arena (indoor, no weather risk); the Barcelona home record is only 3-2.

games.reason: Barcelona are the clear on-paper favourite: the better record and point difference, at home, and the books price them at about 75%. The confidence is low because the Polymarket price dropped 12% in 24 hours (0.73 to 0.64, mostly at 12:00 UTC on 16 Nov) with no explanatory news found, because Barcelona are missing their top scorer Punter plus Gibson, Evbuomwan and Makoundou with Nunez doubtful, and because the visitor won each of the last four meetings by double digits. Paris are on a four-game winning streak. So p is trimmed below the market within 5 points.
games.main_risk: Paris keep scoring against a Barcelona side without Punter, Gibson and Evbuomwan, with Nunez doubtful, and win or keep it close; the favourite's unexplained price drop (-12% in 24h) could reflect information I did not find, such as a late injury or lineup news.

checks.team_news: Afternoon re-check (Tue 17 Nov, 14:25 UTC). Eurohoops' official EuroLeague Round 12 injury report (17 Nov) lists, for Baskonia, Kenneth Faried (left thigh, hurt in Round 11) and Marcio Santos (last played in Round 9). Sedekerskis is not in the part of the report I could read, but the morning Infobae/EFE preview named him out. For Hapoel it lists Tomas Satoransky as having missed Round 10 with a head injury and returned in Round 11, so he is no longer a worry. It lists Bruno Caboclo as last playing in Round 10 and not on the Round 11 gameday roster, so he is probably out again. That is a small negative, since he is a rotation big. Vasilije Micic is NOT in the report, so no new injury is declared. His groin problem of 9 Nov is not confirmed away, but he played on 12 Nov. Tyler Ennis (Achilles) was out in the morning report and I found no change. No late illness or coach comments found. Still no official lineups.
checks.lineups: Not out yet (official fives come about 60 min before tip-off, after this check). Expected Hapoel core: Micic, Elijah Bryant, Antonio Blakeney, Dan Oturu, probably without Caboclo and Ennis. Baskonia: thin and rebuilt, with Smits and Kamenjas due to debut.
checks.rotation: Unchanged from the morning. Baskonia played the ACB on Sun 15 Nov (lost 84-98 to Real Madrid), so 2 days of rest. Hapoel last played on 12 Nov (5 days of rest) and travel to Vitoria. No sign of a rest day for starters.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Baskonia 1-11, last, wanting a second win. Hapoel 6-5, 10th, on a 3-game losing run and fighting for the top-10 line. The nothing-to-play-for rule is not triggered. Coach Perasovic was appointed on 14 Oct.
checks.form: Unchanged. Baskonia 0-5 in their last five and 0-5 away, margin -12.0, the worst offence in the league. Hapoel margin +3.2, 90.4 points scored, but they lost 73-80 at Maccabi on 12 Nov and lost the Winner Cup final on 9 Nov after leading by 23.
checks.h2h: 1-1 in 2025-26: Hapoel won 114-89 in Nov 2025, Baskonia won 118-109 on 27 Mar 2026 (behind closed doors). Both high scoring. Hapoel's high turnovers and Baskonia's offensive rebounding keep an upset in play.
checks.odds: Hapoel prices: first listed 0.625 (about $37 traded then), last night 0.625-0.635, this morning 0.765, LIVE now 0.705 (about $1,100 traded today, swinging between about 0.62 and 0.78). So it is up 8 points (+12.8%) from the first listing, but down 6 points (-7.8%) from this morning. I found no news that explains the afternoon fall. Most likely the market is retracing the thin-market spike toward the bookmakers' range, now helped by real volume. The one adverse piece of news I did find is Caboclo's likely absence, which is small and cannot account for 6 points. The last bookmaker prices I have are from last night, not fresh: FanDuel -300/+225 (de-vigged about 70.9%) and Bet-Experts 1.34/3.92 (about 74.5%). I could not find a fresh bookmaker quote this afternoon. Live 0.705 sits inside that 71-74.5% range, so the market and the bookmakers broadly agree. The favourite's price is not down 3% or more from p_first, so the low-confidence price rule is not triggered. The line was -6.5 at about 0.50 last night, total 181.5.
checks.models: Unchanged. Basketballsphere season margins: Hapoel +3.2 vs Baskonia -12.0 (15-point gap), pick Hapoel -5.5. This points to a clear but not huge Hapoel win, consistent with about 70%.
checks.venue_weather: Fernando Buesa Arena, Vitoria-Gasteiz, 20:30 CET (19:30 UTC), EuroLeague Round 12. Fans ARE admitted: Gasteiz Hoy (17 Nov) reports the game will have a crowd, but only season-ticket holders with ID, no ticket sales, doors open 90 minutes early for security checks. The special bus line was suspended for security reasons. A large security deployment is expected, and Indar Baskonia called a total boycott. A protest is called at 19:00 at the Virgen Blanca. In March this fixture was behind closed doors. That is different now: a partial, subdued home crowd and a tense atmosphere, a small unknown, with no clear edge either way. Indoor, weather irrelevant.

games.reason: Hapoel remain a clear favourite: 6-5 and +3.2 margin against a 1-11 Baskonia at -12.0, with Faried, Santos and Sedekerskis out, the weakest offence in the league and two debutants still integrating. Satoransky is back and Micic is not on the official injury report. Caboclo is probably out (small negative) and no lineups are confirmed. The 0.765 to 0.705 fall this afternoon has no news behind it and looks like a thin-market spike being corrected toward the bookmakers' 71-74.5%. The live price is still well above the first listing, so the favourite has not lost ground against p_first. p is set at 0.70, just under the market, because of the Caboclo and Micic uncertainty, Hapoel's 3-game losing run and the bounce risk of a new-coach Baskonia. Confidence stays medium because lineups are unconfirmed and I have no fresh bookmaker price.
games.main_risk: A Micic groin relapse (no official confirmation either way), Caboclo's absence, Hapoel's three straight defeats and high turnovers, and a Baskonia side with new signings that is dangerous on offensive rebounds. Hapoel at -6.5 is priced about even, so an outright win is likelier than covering. The market swung 0.62-0.78 today and could still move. Lineups only appear after this check.

games.reason: Hard rule 'favourite has nothing left to play for and the opponent does'.
